common_part.cm4_title: Brain-Charting Autism and Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Reveals Distinct and Overlapping Neurobiology

cm6_clarity_of_research_objectives.reason: The research objectives are clearly stated. The study aims to characterize cortical anatomy associated with autism and ADHD using population modeling, examine sources of variability related to sex, age, and autistic/ADHD traits, and investigate co-occurring autism and ADHD. The application purpose of normative modeling is explicitly described as providing a framework for studying diverse conditions in reference to a common baseline to quantify individual differences and address heterogeneity.
cm6_clarity_of_research_objectives.supporting_text: Here, we leveraged models of average brain development previously characterized by our group (98) to quantify alterations related to autism and ADHD. To our knowledge, this is the first study to use population modeling to investigate gray matter alterations related to these conditions in comparison to a common reference sample. We examined sources of variability related to sex, age, and measures of autistic and ADHD traits. Finally, we examined whether a subset of individuals with cooccurring autism and ADHD presented with distinct alterations.

common_part.cm7_additional_comments: This study uses an existing normative model (BrainCharts) developed by Bethlehem et al. (2022) rather than building a new normative model. The study applies this existing model to characterize deviations in autism and ADHD populations. The large multi-site dataset (N=4255 after QC) from 7 datasets across 49 sites is a major strength.

nm1_clear_definition_of_target_populatio.reason: The study uses existing datasets with well-documented demographic characteristics. Age (2-64 years, mean 14.0, median 12.4), sex (687 female and 1182 male controls; 270 female and 717 male ADHD; 288 female and 1111 male autism), and sample sizes are clearly specified. Diagnostic information is based on primary diagnoses from each contributing dataset, which have established diagnostic procedures. The reasons for selecting these datasets are implicitly clear - they are major publicly available and well-characterized neuroimaging datasets for autism and ADHD research.
nm1_clear_definition_of_target_populatio.supporting_text: T1-weighted scans were combined from 49 sites across 7 datasets, including the ABIDE (Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange) (102,103), the POND (Province of Ontario Neurodevelopmental) Network, the HBN (Healthy Brain Network) at the Child Mind Institute (104), the ADHD200 Consortium, the Multimodal Developmental Neurogenetics of Females with ASD dataset from the National Institute of Mental Health Data Archive, the UK MRC-AIMS (Medical Research Council Autism Imaging Multi-centre Study), and the University of California San Diego Biomarkers of Autism study. The final dataset after quality control (QC) included 4255 individuals (1869 typically developing control participants [687 female, 1182 male], 987 individuals with ADHD [270 female, 717 male], and 1399 autistic individuals [288 female, 1111 male], ages 2-64 years [mean 14.0, median 12.4]).

nm2_clarity_of_inclusion_and_exclusion_c.reason: The inclusion criteria are clearly described - individuals with MRI data and a primary diagnosis of autism or ADHD or no diagnosis were included. Image quality requirements are extensively described with manual QC using FSQC tool with cutoff of 2.5, evaluation of surface reconstruction and raw scan quality including motion artifacts. The Euler number was included as a covariate to account for residual quality variations. Number of subjects included in final analysis (N=4255 after QC from initial 4736 before QC) is specified. Exclusion is based on quality control procedures.
nm2_clarity_of_inclusion_and_exclusion_c.supporting_text: Individuals with magnetic resonance imaging data and a primary diagnosis of autism or ADHD or no diagnosis were included... All scans underwent manual QC of raw image and FreeSurfer surface reconstructions using our FSQC tool (107), which allows for the evaluation of both surface reconstruction and raw scan quality, including motion artifacts (108). A cutoff of 2.5 was used for FSQC (107). nm3_handling_of_confounding_variables.reason: The study comprehensively addresses confounding variables. Age and sex are accounted for in the normative models. Site effects are handled through a two-step process: (1) ComBat harmonization was applied across all sites with age, sex, and diagnosis preserved as covariates, and (2) the GAMLSS models themselves account for site/scanner-specific variables. The treatment of covariates in normative modeling is clearly described - out-of-sample centile scores were generated accounting for age, sex, and site/scanner effects. Additionally, Euler number was included as a covariate in all analyses to control for residual image quality variations.
nm3_handling_of_confounding_variables.supporting_text: Sex-specific life span developmental trajectories for each neuroanatomical measure were estimated using generalized additive models of location scale and shape (GAMLSS) for a sample of 75,241 typically developing (TD) individuals, accounting for site- and scanner-specific variables (98)... ComBat was applied to the entire dataset across all global and regional measures, with each site treated as a batch and with covariates of age, sex, and diagnosis to preserve related biological variation... Because even small variations in quality can bias downstream analyses (108,109), we also included the FreeSurfer-derived Euler number (110) as a covariate in all analyses.
